**Test image observations:**
- A distinct strip/patch of completely dead, brown, dried plants in the center of a soybean row
- Surrounding plants are healthy and green
- Whole-plant death with brown, desiccated stems and leaves collapsed
- Field-level patch pattern of wilting/death

**Candidate reasoning:**
The pattern of dead plants in a discrete field patch, with complete plant death (not just leaf lesions), strongly suggests a soil-borne root/crown disease. The top-left panel of the Sudden Death Syndrome reference image is an almost identical match — showing a strip of dead/dying plants in a field row surrounded by healthy green plants, exactly as seen in the test image. SDS causes root rot followed by foliar symptoms and eventually whole-plant death in field patches.
